gates.text: Truth: no claim, number, metric, milestone, screenshot, customer or quote that isn't in confirmed facts or cited research. Gaps are written around (pick an angle the confirmed facts fully support); never an invention, never a placeholder in publishable copy.

Limits and format: every post is 280 characters or fewer (unless the brief says Premium, in which case the first 280 stand alone); threads are 4-8 posts; 0-2 hashtags; no link in the hook post; at most one exclamation mark per post.
Policy: no engagement bait, no fake or mocked-up screenshots, no impersonation or misleading quote-posts, no banned phrases from copy-fundamentals; every image has alt text.

anchors.1: Padding, filler words, throat-clearing; obvious cuts available.
anchors.3: Tight-ish, but a few words or a clause could go without loss.
anchors.5: Every word earns its place; quotable as written; nothing can be cut without losing meaning.

anchors.1: "🧵 THREAD", hype listicle opener or a generic truth.
anchors.3: Clear topic but no number, finding or tension.
anchors.5: A specific number, claim or finding in the first line that works on its own and is paid off.

anchors.1: Opinions or tips with no evidence; could come from anyone.
anchors.3: Some specifics but the central claim lacks a number or first-hand detail.
anchors.5: Central claim backed by the business's confirmed number, observation or mechanism inside the post itself.

anchors.3: Useful but expected; a peer would nod and scroll.
anchors.5: A defensible point a knowledgeable peer could argue with or would quote, grounded in evidence.

anchors.1: Posts depend on each other; "This"/"It" openers; padded single idea.
anchors.3: Mostly self-contained, with one or two dependent posts.
anchors.5: Every post works alone if screenshotted; each carries one distinct point; final post lands the takeaway. Score 5 for a single post that fully stands alone.

anchors.1: Link in the hook post, or a vague "check it out".
anchors.5: Hook link-free; link in a reply or final post with one line on what it is; at most one ask.

anchors.1: Brand-speak, hype or emoji decoration; off-positioning.
anchors.3: Clean but generic; not tied to a positioning element.
anchors.5: Sounds like a sharp, specific person; expresses one positioning element in the customer's words.

anchors.1: Pasted from another channel; fake or stock visuals; no alt text.
anchors.3: Written for X but visuals or alt text vague; no channel-fit note where one was needed.
anchors.5: Native to X (length, rhythm, reply-ready); real screenshots or charts of confirmed data with alt text; channel-fit note when the business is local.
